We need to imagine three experts each proposing one test case per method, share, then proceed, but final answer is a complete JUnit 4 test file for the given class, covering typical use cases, edge cases, error scenarios. The test file should start with ###Test START## and end with ###Test END##. Provide JUnit 4 test class DocumentTest.java.

We need to test many methods: constructor, createShell, location, head, body, title getter/setter, createElement, normalise (including moving text nodes, duplicate head/body, ensureMetaCharsetElement), findFirstElementByTagName (private, but indirectly via head/body), outerHtml, text override, nodeName, charset related methods (charset, updateMetaCharsetElement, ensureMetaCharsetElement behavior), outputSettings getters/setters, quirksMode, clone.

Also test error scenarios: createShell with null baseUri should throw exception, title(null) should throw NPE via Validate.notNull, etc.

We need to use JUnit 4, i.e., @Test, @Before, assertEquals, assertNotNull, etc. Use Jsoup classes? The Document class depends on other classes like Element, Node, etc., which are part of Jsoup. We can use Jsoup library, but in test we can instantiate Document directly.

We'll need to import org.jsoup.nodes.*; org.jsoup.parser.Tag; org.jsoup.helper.Validate; etc.

Test typical: Document doc = new Document("http://example.com"); assertEquals("http://example.com", doc.location());

Test createShell: Document shell = Document.createShell("http://example.com"); assertNotNull(shell.head()); assertNotNull(shell.body()); assertEquals("head", shell.head().tagName()); etc.

Test title: doc.title("My Title"); assertEquals("My Title", doc.title()); also test that title trims whitespace and normalises.

Test title null: expect IllegalArgumentException (Validate.notNull throws IllegalArgumentException). So test that.

Test createElement: Element a = doc.createElement("a"); assertEquals("a", a.tagName()); assertEquals(doc.baseUri(), a.baseUri());

Test normalise: Build doc with stray text nodes and duplicate head/body, then call normalise and verify structure.

Test ensureMetaCharsetElement: set updateMetaCharsetElement(true), set outputSettings syntax to html, set charset to UTF-8, call charset(Charset.forName("ISO-8859-1")) and ensure meta element exists with correct charset and no obsolete meta[name=charset].

Test xml syntax: set outputSettings.syntax(OutputSettings.Syntax.xml), call charset, verify XmlDeclaration at first child with correct attributes.

Test clone: Document cloned = doc.clone(); assertNotSame(doc, cloned); assertEquals(doc.charset(), cloned.charset()); also ensure outputSettings cloned.

Test outputSettings setter and getter.

Test quirksMode.

Test outerHtml returns same as html().

Test text override: doc.text("Hello"); assertEquals("Hello", doc.body().text());

Edge: normalise when no html element exists.

Error: createShell with null baseUri throws IllegalArgumentException.

But Document extends Element, but its root is "#root". When we call doc.appendElement("html") we get html under root.

In normalise test, we can directly add extra head and body.

e.g., Document doc = new Document("http://example.com"); doc.appendElement("html"); Element head1 = doc.appendElement("head"); head1.appendElement("title").text("Title1"); Element head2 = doc.appendElement("head"); head2.appendElement("meta").attr("charset","UTF-8"); // duplicate head.

Similarly duplicate body.

Add stray text nodes at root and html.

Then call doc.normalise();

Check that only one head and body, contents merged.

Check that stray text moved to body.

Test meta charset ensure: after charset change, meta charset element is present with correct value.

Ok.

We need to annotate @Test(expected = IllegalArgumentException.class) for error cases.

Make sure we import java.nio.charset.Charset.

We may need to use org.junit.*.

We'll also need to use org.jsoup.Jsoup for parsing? Not needed.

We need to use org.jsoup.select.Elements for selecting meta.

Alright.
